## Linear Systems and Rank

::: {#exr-la-structured-system name="A Structured Homogeneous System"}

Consider the homogeneous linear system

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{n} a_jx_j+bx_i=0,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
$$

where $\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\ne0$. Determine the conditions on $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and $b$ under which:

a. The system has only the zero solution.
b. The system has nonzero solutions. In this case, determine its solution set.

:::

::: {#exr-la-product-rank name="Rank of a Matrix Product"}

Let $A$ and $B$ be $n\times n$ matrices. Prove both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{rank}(L_{AB})
&\ge \operatorname{rank}(L_A)+\operatorname{rank}(L_B)-n,\\
\operatorname{rank}(L_{AB})
&\le \min\{\operatorname{rank}(L_A),\operatorname{rank}(L_B)\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

::: {#exr-la-sum-rank name="Rank of a Matrix Sum"}

Let $A$ and $B$ be $n\times m$ matrices. Prove

$$
\operatorname{rank}(L_{A+B})
\le \operatorname{rank}(L_A)+\operatorname{rank}(L_B).
$$

:::

::: {#exr-la-annihilation name="Rank Under Mutual Annihilation"}

Let $A,B\in M_{n\times n}(\mathbb R)$. Suppose $AB=BA=0$ and $\operatorname{rank}(A^2)=\operatorname{rank}(A)$. Prove

$$
\operatorname{rank}(A+B)=\operatorname{rank}(A)+\operatorname{rank}(B).
$$

:::

::: {#exr-la-commuting-rank name="Commuting Matrices"}

Let $A,B,C,D$ be pairwise commuting $n\times n$ matrices satisfying $AC+BD=I_n$. Prove

$$
\operatorname{rank}(AB)=\operatorname{rank}(A)+\operatorname{rank}(B)-n.
$$

:::

::: {#exr-la-transpose name="A Matrix and Its Transpose"}

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix satisfying $AA^t=k^2I_n$, where $k\in\mathbb R$. Prove

$$
\operatorname{rank}(kI_n-A)=\operatorname{rank}\big((kI_n-A)^2\big).
$$

:::

::: {#exr-la-square-zero name="A Square-Zero Matrix"}

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with rank $r$, where $1\le r\le n/2$, and suppose $A^2=0$. Prove that an invertible matrix $P$ exists such that

$$
A=P
\begin{pmatrix}
0&I_r&0\\
0&0&0\\
0&0&0
\end{pmatrix}
P^{-1},
$$

where $I_r$ is the $r\times r$ identity matrix and each $0$ denotes a zero matrix of the appropriate size.

:::

## Eigenvalues and Canonical Forms

::: {#exr-la-involution name="An Involution"}

Let $A$ be a real square matrix satisfying $A^2=I_n$. Prove that $A$ is diagonalizable.

:::

::: {#exr-la-self-adjoint name="Commuting Self-Adjoint Operators"}

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and let $U$ and $T$ be self-adjoint linear operators on $V$ satisfying $UT=TU$.

Prove that $V$ has an orthonormal basis consisting of common eigenvectors of $U$ and $T$.

:::

::: {#exr-la-triangularization name="Simultaneous Triangularization"}

Let $A$ and $B$ be $n\times n$ complex matrices satisfying $AB=A+B$.

Prove that $A$ and $B$ are simultaneously triangularizable: there is a basis in which both matrices are upper triangular.

:::

::: {#exr-la-polynomial name="A Polynomial Constraint"}

Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{m}b_iA^i=0,
\qquad
|b_m|>\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}|b_i|.
$$

Prove that the equation $2X-XA^2=AX$ has only the trivial solution $X=0$.

:::
